judged/historyComment.subject: code comment
judged/historyComment.instructions: HISTORY means the comment narrates the code's own past: an earlier behaviour that no longer holds ('this used to retry', 'before X this read argv', 'we switched to Y'), or which change, review, pass or person altered it. TODAY means anything else: what the code does, why, a constraint, or a noun phrase naming a purpose. 'X used to <verb>' meaning 'X that is used for <verb>ing' is TODAY.

criteria.today: states what the code does now, or why, or a purpose, or shows data
criteria.history: tells the code's past: what it used to do, what changed it, when or by whom

judged/historyComment.message: the comment tells the code's history: say what it does today and why; how it got here lives in git log

judged/commentClaimsCode.subject: comment and the code it sits on
judged/commentClaimsCode.instructions: Read the comment, then the code it sits on, given after it. OVERCLAIMS means the comment states something about that code which the code shown does not do or contradicts: a wider scope, a number or bound, an order, a guarantee, a case it handles, a caller, an argument or a behaviour that the code plainly lacks or does differently. HOLDS means every claim the comment makes that the code shown can prove or disprove is true of it. A claim about something outside the code shown (a reason, a caller elsewhere, the wider system) cannot be checked here and HOLDS; so does a comment that is vague or tells less than the code does. A number the code has, said in other words, HOLDS, and so does a number that is not the code's own value: one derived from it with other inputs, another thing's value it is compared with or explained against (an engine's default, a margin under a target, a measurement). OVERCLAIMS needs the code shown to state the same quantity, name or case differently, or to plainly lack what the comment says it does.

criteria.holds: every claim the comment makes that the code shown can check is true of that code
criteria.overclaims: the comment claims a scope, number, guarantee, caller or behaviour the code shown lacks or contradicts

judged/commentClaimsCode.message: the comment claims more than the code under it does: make it say what the code does, or the code do what it says

judged/testOracle.subject: test case
judged/testOracle.instructions: The item is one test case, after its file's imports. TAUTOLOGICAL means the test's expected value is computed by the code under test itself, or the data it checks is built by the very function whose defect the test must catch, so the test passes even when that function is wrong: for example the expectation is the same function called again, or a helper made from it, or the fake is laid out with the function the test is about. INDEPENDENT means the expected value is written out (a literal, a fixture stated in full), or computed another way than the code under test, or a property is checked that a defect there would break. Calling the function under test on the actual side only is INDEPENDENT. Judge only what the case shows.

criteria.independent: the expected value is written out or computed apart from the code under test, so a defect there fails the test
criteria.tautological: the expected value or the checked data comes from the code under test, so a defect there passes

judged/testOracle.message: the test's oracle is the code it tests: write the expected value out, or derive it another way

judged/silentDrop.subject: function
judged/silentDrop.instructions: The item is one function, with the comment above it. SILENT means that, given an input or a failure it cannot handle, the function drops it, substitutes a default, or reports success for work it did not do, and says nothing of it: no typed error, no finding, no log line, no field or return type that carries the drop, no comment that names it. SAID means the function refuses with a typed error, reports the case, carries it in its result (an Option, a tagged result, a skip line), or its fallback is said in a comment or a log as deliberate (a documented fail-open), or it drops nothing. An input the function's type or comment says it never receives is not a drop.

criteria.said: every input or failure the function cannot handle is refused, reported, carried in its result or named as a deliberate fallback
criteria.silent: the function drops an input or failure, substitutes a default, or reports work it did not do, with nothing said

judged/silentDrop.message: the function drops what it cannot handle and says nothing: refuse it typed, report it, or name the fallback

judged/scriptSpeech.subject: film beat's speech or picture
judged/scriptSpeech.instructions: The item is what a narrated Bible film says (say:) or shows (picture:) in one beat. The films teach from Scripture alone and never source themselves overtly. BREACH means the words quote or name Ellen White, an Adventist pioneer (Waggoner, Jones, Uriah Smith, William Miller and the like) or one of their books by title, name a denomination or church as an authority, or tell church history (1844, the Millerites, Minneapolis 1888, a church's statement of beliefs), in speech or on screen. CLEAN means anything else: Scripture quoted or retold, "the Bible" named, plain teaching (the Sabbath, the sanctuary, the latter rain, the day of atonement) with no church, person or date of church history named, a pioneer's idea paraphrased with no name, or Bible-era history.

criteria.clean: Scripture, plain teaching or an idea told with no pioneer, book, denomination or church history named
criteria.breach: quotes or names Ellen White, a pioneer or their book, names a denomination, or tells church history

judged/scriptSpeech.message: the beat names its sources or church history: teach it from Scripture, the idea unnamed

patterns.message: Portable core modules must use Effect interfaces. Put host code in an explicit adapter.
core never imports canvas, rive, the house look (style), player, tools, lab or the host's adapters (browser): they import it (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the engine never imports the player, tools, lab or the host's adapters (browser): they import it (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).

the engine declares a rig and draws it (canvas/rive.ts); it never imports the Rive loader or its runtimes (src/rive/), which load a film's rigs for the player and the tools (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the engine never imports the house look (src/style/): the look draws with the engine (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the engine never imports the player, tools, lab or the host's adapters (browser): they import it (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the engine never imports the house look (src/style/): the look draws with the engine (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).

the Rive loader and its runtimes never import the player, tools, lab, the pages' commands or the host's adapters (browser): the player and the tools import them (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).

the Rive loader and its runtimes never import the house look (src/style/): a film's rigs are built from it ahead of time, and the loader loads the built file (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the house look never imports the player, tools, lab, the pages' commands, the Rive loader (src/rive/) or the host's adapters (browser): they may import it (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the engine never imports the player, tools or lab: they import it (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the player never imports the tools or the lab: the lab mounts the player (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
a page reaches the host through its services: only a page's mount builds the host (`BrowserHost`, browser/host-browser.ts), and the stores are storage-browser.ts's.
a page reaches the host through its services: only a page's mount builds the host (`BrowserHost`, browser/host-browser.ts), and the stores are storage-browser.ts's.

an app reaches the film through its package exports (`@bible/film/rive`, `@bible/film/canvas`), never a path into its source: the exports are the film's public modules (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).
the pages' commands never import the player, the tools or the lab: they register their commands with it (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).

no-restricted-properties.message: Make the id with uniqueId(ChangeId) (packages/film/src/core/unique.ts), or decode one that came over the wire: an id written by hand can be another change's.
Make the id with uniqueId(RequestId) (packages/film/src/core/unique.ts), or decode one that came over the wire: an id written by hand can be another request's.
Make the id with uniqueId(OpId) (packages/film/src/core/unique.ts), or decode one that came over the wire: an id written by hand can be another run's.

patterns.message: the host's adapters never import the player, the tools or the lab: the pages import them (packages/film/README.md, the purity rule).

fetch.use: the page's LabClient (packages/film/src/lab/api.ts) or Effect's HttpClient

EventSource.use: the page's LabClient (packages/film/src/lab/api.ts) or Effect's HttpClient

XMLHttpRequest.use: the page's LabClient (packages/film/src/lab/api.ts) or Effect's HttpClient

navigator.use: the page's HttpClient, not a beacon the harness cannot see

setTimeout.use: Effect.sleep on the host's Clock (timersOn, packages/film/src/player/throttle.ts)

setInterval.use: Effect.sleep on the host's Clock (timersOn, packages/film/src/player/throttle.ts)

requestIdleCallback.use: Effect.sleep on the host's Clock (timersOn, packages/film/src/player/throttle.ts)

matchMedia.use: the host's Viewport (packages/film/src/browser/viewport.ts; useMatches in a component): a server render answers as a phone

innerWidth.use: the studio's one breakpoint: the host's Viewport (packages/film/src/browser/viewport.ts), PHONE and WIDE (packages/film/src/lab/viewport.ts)

outerWidth.use: the studio's one breakpoint: the host's Viewport (packages/film/src/browser/viewport.ts), PHONE and WIDE (packages/film/src/lab/viewport.ts)
